“Since I was little, I was taught to be respectful of everyone; we should learn this lesson,” he told the crowd.

Sports.title: Manchester United start new signing Andrey Santos in pre-season loss to Wrexham
Sports.content:
Andrey Santos made a bright first Manchester United appearance as they lost 1-0 in a pre-season friendly against Wrexham in Helsinki. Sam Smith scored the only goal with an easy finish six minutes before half-time, minutes after heading against his own crossbar defending a corner.

United were without the players who have featured at the World Cup, including their new signing Youri Tielemans, as well as Benjamin Sesko, but Michael Carrick put out a strong starting XI in front of 20,000 spectators.

Santos, who became United’s first summer signing when he joined from Chelsea at the start of the week for an initial £48m, took his place at the base of midfield alongside Mason Mount.

Carrick had praised the Brazilian’s attitude before the match, saying: “He’s a fantastic character. He’s settled in so quickly and he’s buzzing to be here”

The 22-year-old soon settled in, showing a good range of passing and winning several duels in a busy display. However, Wrexham, who played their first pre-season friendly against Wisla Krakow last weekend, were looking brighter and threatened when Bailey Cadamarteri nicked the ball off Ayden Heaven before the defender recovered.

United’s first chance was a Joshua Zirkzee shot that fizzed wide in the 24th minute and they almost went ahead when Smith tried to clear a corner but hit the bar in the 36th minute. Smith was soon on the scoresheet, tapping in after Lewis O’Brien’s cross appeared to go through Harry Maguire’s legs.

Twenty one of the 22 players were replaced at half-time, with only Wrexham’s Aaron James staying on, and Carrick sent out a side of academy products against a Wrexham team including Conor Coady and Kieffer Moore.

View image in fullscreen Michael Carrick applauds the fans at the end of the pre-season friendly match against Wrexham at Helsingin Olympiastadion. Photograph: Ash Donelon/Manchester United/Getty Images

United dominated the ball but struggled to fashion chances as the pace of the game dropped. Wrexham threatened with a low shot from Davis Keillor-Dunn but Radek Vitek made the save.

When Ethan Wheatley prodded Harry Amass’s cross goalwards in the 78th minute, it was their first shot on target but Dan Ward made the save before holding a low drive from Shea Lacey.

Sports.title: Hart, Rooney and Richards on rowing the Hudson and if Tuchel should keep his job
Sports.content:
The BBC punditry trio Wayne Rooney, Micah Richards and Joe Hart are fresh off a boat on New York’s Hudson River after an attempt to honour Rooney’s declaration that he would “row the River Mersey” if Norway reached the World Cup quarter-final. They did, prompting Erling Haaland to tease Rooney, saying: “I’m looking forward to seeing you, Wayney boy.”

How was it?

Wayne Rooney: “It was more relaxing than I thought. Once we got into a nice little rhythm, we were OK. A couple of other times we came out of the rhythm and Micah nearly killed my back. But no, it was good. Harty looks like he’s been doing it for years. So it was actually enjoyable.”

Micah Richards: “It was good fun. I wouldn’t pick it to do it again, but I enjoyed it – there for the lads.”

Joe Hart: “It sums up how we’ve been the whole World Cup, as a trio. None of us were so comfy doing it but no one cared, we all got on with it and it was a good laugh. And Wazza said he was going to do it and he has done it, so he’s a man of his word.”

Their first time working together at the World Cup was England’s second group game, the goalless draw with Ghana on 23 June, but it revealed an instant chemistry between the three.

JH: “It’s gone well because, while we’re all very professional in what we’re doing, we also go way back – like a long way back – and that’s important. It means that we’re ourselves and feel comfortable around each other. Gabby [Logan], Kelly [Cates] and Chappers [Mark Chapman] have been unreal as presenters in getting the best out of us. As a group we’ve really found something.”

WR: “It’s strange in a way, but it’s very similar to when you’re playing on the pitch. We all have our bits of analysis to do but in terms of when we’re talking, you don’t want to speak over someone else, so it’s about eye contact and understanding when you’re coming in next. It’s really good chemistry.”

View image in fullscreen Joe Hart (left) and Wayne Rooney (centre) talk to Mark Chapman in Atlanta during the World Cup semi-final between England and Argentina. Photograph: Javier García/Shutterstock

How far do you go back?

MR: “Harty – for me, it would have been when you arrived [at Manchester City] from Shrewsbury [in 2006], wouldn’t it?”

JH: “I met Micah when I was 19, he was 18 – so over 20 years ago. And then obviously Wayne was in the England team from when he was like 12 [laughs].”

WR: “I met you, Micah, the first time you were in the England squad [November 2006] and I remember thinking: ‘Who’s this loud lad coming in?’ So we’ve played with and against each other, we enjoy each other’s company and we’ve all had different careers in different ways and are very respectful of what we’ve achieved and, most importantly, now what we’re doing.

“We’re respectful of each other’s opinions. And what helps, too, is that before the show there’s a lot of preparation – we try to talk and help each other out alongside the producers, who do it so well.”

How easy is it to be as honest as you all are when offering opinions?

JH: “I find it easy because no one’s right. You may say your opinion isn’t as valid as mine because you haven’t played the game. But I don’t think it matters – as long as you’re being fair, then fine. I’ll die on my sword for this but I’ll always represent the players because I feel like you can’t forget what it’s like to be out there. That’s not giving them excuses, but explaining why certain things happen because, especially at the World Cup, the level is unbelievable. So it’d be lazy to say someone’s not a good player. But there’s reasons why they may have difficult games and usually it’s down to the opposition or circumstances. So it’s just about trying to paint that picture as best you can from a professional point of view.”

MR: “From my point of view, Joe and Wayne deserve huge credit for the way they’ve applied themselves and performed because with the BBC, there have been as many as 24 million viewers. This is your first tournament Wayne, I believe?

WR: “Well, I’ve done a couple of games before.”

MR: “Your first when you’re doing it properly, then, and you’re on every single time. And Joe as well – you did a little bit of the last Euros, didn’t you?”

JH: “I’ve done pitch-side stuff before.”

MR: “So for them to be in the studio and perform the way they are, I think it’s sensational. It’s very hard, especially when you’re in Salford and we all see ITV’s fancy studio [in New York] – we have to work a little bit harder to keep the audience engaged.”

WR: “Just on that – ITV [their experts] haven’t been to a game, have they? We’ve been here for three days and already been to more than them [England’s semi-final]!”

MR: “Our chemistry – we’ve just come out of the dressing room, haven’t we? We’ve still got that banter and we want to be relatable on air. We know broadcasting can be difficult at times but going back to your question about honesty: we’re just honest, you know, the same on air as off.”

WR: “There’s a good blend between us. Joe’s completely right about defending the players as well. There’s times where we’ve all been criticised when we were players and it’s not nice. But from my point of view I don’t mind criticising but as long as it’s constructive and it’s in the right way. Like when I’ve said a player has not had a good game: I’ll say that if I feel the player will know he has not had a good game.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“Like after the last game [England’s 2-1 defeat by Argentina] – I felt it was a mistake by Thomas Tuchel to go defensive. It’s important to say that because if you are sitting at home and you say the players were brilliant when they were not or Tuchel was brilliant when he wasn’t, then you know you’re not going to listen to what we say.”

View image in fullscreen Thomas Tuchel made mistakes in England’s semi-final defeat by Argentina, according to Rooney. Photograph: Simon M Bruty/Getty Images

You were certainly relatable after Harry Kane’s voice went squeaky following England’s 3-2 last-16 win over Mexico

JH: “I had to strap in because they’d fully gone and I thought: ‘They’re going to come back to us here.’ So I didn’t enjoy it as much as I’d like to have.”

WR: “I was looking for Kermit the Frog! No, I thought it was brilliant. Kelly [Somers] was interviewing him and Harry could have stopped the interview a bit earlier but fair play, he didn’t – it was so funny.”

JH: “That night was special. The fact there was an hour delay [because of the weather] and we ended up kicking off at 2am UK time and that could have been a difficult slog, couldn’t it?”

WR: “But even that – we planned for a delay as well, actually planned for more than two hours.”

Your sense of humour, Wayne, was also evident in you taking Haaland’s “Wayney boy” in good spirit

WR: “We had good fun doing it and we just sent a message to Haaland, saying ‘Enjoy your time in Marbella’ and obviously, too, that we hope he enjoys the boat. I said I’d do it and straight away I was thinking, ‘I’m in trouble here’ but Micah and Harty helped me out. We just enjoy each other’s company. We’re going to play padel now together and so it’s important that the people you work with you like.”

View image in fullscreen Severe weather delayed Mexico’s match against England, but local fans – and the BBC pundits in the studio – had arrived prepared. Photograph: Daniel Becerril/Reuters

England play France in Saturday’s bronze-medal game. How hard would it be to stay motivated for a game like that?

JH: “If I was going for a Golden Boot like Harry then I’d definitely [be motivated]. You’ve got to create a narrative. It’s obviously easy for us to joke and say it’s a pointless game, but if you’re in that England camp and representing your country on the biggest stage, then do it. That’s where Tuchel has still got to be a top manager, a top motivator.”

Should Tuchel remain in the job?

MR: “Yes – though I would have liked to see him go for it more against Argentina.”

JH: “I’m going to reserve my opinion – I want to hear his verdict. We were there that night and it got really wild. England were toe-to-toe with the best team in the world with the medals to prove it and the best player to ever play the game [Lionel Messi]. Then I felt like it was drifting away - Tuchel may have got caught up in the moment as a human and just thought: ‘Revert to type to what got us through [against Mexico].’ I think that’s something he’ll reflect on.”

WR: “It was there for us to win with 15, 20 minutes to go, whatever it was. He made a big mistake in not allowing us the opportunity to get more pressure on the ball and surrender possession. But if Tuchel gets sacked who are we going to bring in? You could get Pep [Guardiola] but is that going to work? Tuchel will learn from his mistakes so I would keep him.”

MR: “I agree with Wayne in terms of the manager and the negative moves he made on the day [but] Argentina were the better team. The players showed pride but I watched that second half again and they absolutely battered us.”

Rooney, Hart and Richards will cover the World Cup final live on BBC One and iPlayer on Sunday.

Sports.title: France 4-6 England: Three Lions win World Cup wooden spoon with bonkers but brilliant performance that might just vindicate Thomas Tuchel, writes CRAIG HOPE
Sports.content:
There is no doubting Thomas. At least, that is, if you are Thomas.

For Tuchel, this absurdly bi-polar victory will be vindication, silencing the boos that tarnished his name before kick-off and the chorus of criticism that has followed him since Wednesday’s semi-final defeat by Argentina. He has delivered England’s best World Cup finish since 1966. Not quite the second star he promised, but a first bronze medal. With the German, it will always be his way or the freeway.

But for those who have formed that mass choir of inspection in recent days, they too will see this as justification. Look what happens when you attack a lead rather than defend it, Thomas? For them, there will be regret. There will be anger, even, at a 6-4 win over the tournament favourites. They will also point to England’s second-half collapse as evidence of tactical cowardice and an inevitable retreat. That is what this flash referendum on the country's head coach has caused amid the fallout of Argentina.

Tuchel called the split among supporters ’50-50’ on the eve of the game, an interpretation that was both favourable and naive. When his appearance on the big screen stirred jeers from a Miami crowd of far more white than blue, it would have stung.

But the response of his team was louder still, and that moved both the manager and his assistant Anthony Barry. At half-time, with the score at a barely believable 4-0 to England, Barry said: 'I can't find the words about how proud I am of those players. We're playing a game with broken hearts, 11 lads with broken hearts.

‘I've seen them in the hotel in the last few days with broken hearts. The cynics will say it's too late but we still play against a world-class opponent and I'm so proud of the boys.’

Bukayo Saka netted a hat-trick to help England secure their best World Cup finish since 1966

After defeat to Argentina on Wednesday, England competed with 'broken hearts' to claim third place in Miami

Kylian Mbappe was unable to help France end on a high in an eye-popping end to both nations' World Cup journey

The cynics will say it is too late. Where was this bravery when it was needed at 1-0 up in Atlanta? Where was Bukayo Saka against Argentina? Here he was sending Theo Hernandez for the baguettes every time he got the ball. So much so, the full-back was hooked at half-time. Saka had scored twice by then. Come the end, he had a hat-trick. Individually and collectively, England were inspired. At least for 45 minutes they were.

We had, mistakenly, thought that Tuchel’s performance in his pre-match press conference would be more significant than anything that played out on the pitch. There, we got an insight into his thinking having had time to reflect on Argentina. And his thinking was exactly the same as it was in the immediate aftermath - England’s exit was not on him. Yes, he would take responsibility, but he was not responsible. There is a subtle difference, yet it is one that would have landed like a sledgehammer in the dressing-room. After parking the bus in Atlanta, this felt like he was chucking his players under it.

Tuchel’s subsequent team selection had an uneasy whiff of self-preservation. Seven changes and no Harry Kane or Jude Bellingham. Surely we could not criticise him if the reserves did not perform? France had Kylian Mbappe and Michael Olise in their XI.

England’s start, then, was a shock. They played with freedom, adventure and precision. Goodness, they were brave on the ball. When they took the lead in the third minute, it was overdue, such was the purpose with which they began.

Declan Rice intercepted a ball on halfway and, when France’s efforts to recover the situation amounted to nothing more than a Gallic shrug, the midfielder took that as an invitation. He drove into the space in front of him, composed himself 25 yards out and slammed into the bottom corner.

Thomas Tuchel received heaping criticisms after defeat to Argentina and was somewhat subdued in Miami

Didier Deschamps oversaw his last ever match in the France dugout but could not see out a final win

Declan Rice was the first name on the scoresheet just minutes after the match kicked off

Mbappe did at least help bolster his Golden Boot credentials by establishing a two-goal lead to contender Lionel Messi

Jude Bellingham was a later substitute and the final scorer as England closed their World Cup chapter Stateside

What to do now? Bring on Dan Burn? Switch to five at the back? There were only 87 minutes to see out. No, England went for a second. They puffed out their chests, gloved up and sought to land another blow. Quick learners, this lot.

Marcus Rashford saw a shot deflected, likewise Saka, who also had a goal disallowed for offside. There were chances at the other end - Dean Henderson saved well from Ryan Cherki - but there would have been France opportunities, too, had England sat back. Instead, here they were, on their feet and marching forward.

In the 18th minute, Rice delivered teasingly from a corner, in a way he had not done since the opening game, and Ezri Konsa flashed a header into the far corner. There were two more before the break and neither goal was at all a surprise. Rashford teed up Saka to finish after the pair burst in behind and Saka rolled an easy fourth after being sprung clear by Eberechi Eze.

Never did we know, however, how dangerous a 4-0 scoreline can be. From the start of the second half, seemingly without instruction from Tuchel, England’s back four set up camp in their own penalty. And so came the invaders.

France 4-6 England: PLAYER RATINGS ENGLAND (4-2-3-1): Henderson 6; Quansah 5, Konsa 5, Guehi 5, Spence 7; Rice 7, Eze 7 (Anderson 79, 6); Saka 9, Rogers 6, Rashford 7 (Watkins 46, 5); Toney 5 (Bellingham 79, 7) Manager: Thomas Tuchel 7 FRANCE (4-2-3-1): Maignan 4; Gusto 3, Konate 4 (Upamecano 46, 6), Lacroix 5, Theo Hernandez 3 (Digne 46, 6); Zaire-Emery 5, Rabiot 5; Olise 7, Cherki 5 (Dembele 46, 7), Doue 5 (Barcola 46, 7); Mbappe 8 Manager: Didier Deschamps 6

Mbappe ran away from Konsa to collect an Olise pass for 4-1. Mbappe turned provider when Bradley Barcola escaped Jarell Quansah for 4-2. Mbappe then finished after France knitted passes around a ragged England, and all of this before the 67th-minute drinks break. At 4-3, you could hear the knives sharpening from across the Atlantic.

But England reached into their own cutlery draw and found a blade of their own. Djed Spence charged into the area in the 86th minute and was tripped by Malo Gusto. Saka stepped up to slot home from the penalty spot for his hat-trick. Ousmane Dembele then smashed a French fourth before Bellingham danced through the goalmouth for England's sixth. With that, the World Cup wooden spoon was theirs.

Tuchel will likely use it to bat away the doubters.

Sports.title: 'Emotionally drained' England coach Anthony Barry appears on the brink of tears during half-time interview as he speaks of Three Lions stars' 'broken hearts' after World Cup exit
Sports.content:
'Emotionally drained' England coach Anthony Barry appears on the brink of tears during half-time interview as he speaks of Three Lions stars' 'broken hearts' after World Cup exit

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

England assistant coach Anthony Barry appeared on the brink of tears as he spoke at half-time about his pride for his Three Lions players after they hit four past France in a jaw-dropping World Cup third-place play-off first-half performance.

It took just three minutes before Declan Rice inked his name on the scoresheet with a curving effort from distance, with Ezri Konsa adding a second 15 minutes later.

Bukayo Saka saw a goal chalked off for offside before he scored his first in the 37th minute, and bagged his brace one minute into added time before the break.

'Have to be honest, there's so much frustration,' Barry said in his final half-time address. 'I'm a little bit emotional, I can't find the words about how proud I am of those players.

'We're playing a game with broken hearts, 11 lads with broken hearts.

Anthony Barry spoke emotionally of his pride in his 'heartbroken' England stars as they scored four in the first-half of their third-place play-off versus France

'I've seen them in the hotel in the last few days with broken hearts. They can build a performance like that by playing through pride for England. The team spirit we've built in the last seven weeks.

'The cynics will say it's too late but we still play against a world-class opponent and I'm so proud of the boys.

'There's 45 minutes to go. The game's not done. Anything can happen. But I'm proud of the team and I hope everyone is as well at home.'

In the BBC studio, Martin Keown suggested that Barry looked 'emotionally drained' after close to two months Stateside.

For fans still distressed at missing out on a place in a World Cup final, the bronze-medal match may appear to have little significance.

But with honour still on the table, France may look to step up their performance in the second-half for outgoing manager Didier Deschamps' final match in charge.

France have not conceded four goals in a single half since their European Championship qualification match against Yugoslavia in 1968.

Captain Kylian Mbappe at times looked bewildered by the ease with which England were able to scythe through France's defence, with Deschamps cutting a desolate figure slumped in the dugout.

Head coach Thomas Tuchel had initially raised eyebrows by opting to start a number of regular fixtures throughout the tournament - such as Declan Rice - while benching others including Jude Bellingham and Harry Kane in Miami.

Sports.title: Now Argentina's RUGBY players mock England after World Cup semi-final victory: Stars wear tribute to 'Hand of God' kit for Nations Championship clash
Sports.content:
Argentina's rugby stars appeared to join the mocking of England after their World Cup victory over their arch-rivals by wearing a kit paying homage to Diego Maradona's 1986 team.

Players wore a jersey similar in colour to that of Argentina's 1986 World Cup-winning side - made famous by Maradona's 'Hand of God' and superb solo goal in a win against England - for their Nations Championship clash in Santiago del Estero.

The Pumas' limited edition kit has been created to mark the 40th anniversary of Argentina lifting their second World Cup.

'With this tribute, the Argentine Rugby Union and Los Pumas celebrate that legacy and renew their commitment to representing Argentina with the same pride, passion, and dedication that distinguish our national teams,' the Argentine Rugby Union said.

England's rugby team had already been forced to switch hotels in Buenos Aires because of the chaos caused by Argentina’s World Cup victory.

Tens of thousands of fans gathered in the Plaza de la República on Wednesday night, celebrating their football team’s 2-1 win over England with a huge street party.

Argentina's rugby stars wore a kit similar to the one worn by Diego Maradona's team in 1986

The jersey was made famous by Diego Maradona's 'Hand of God' en route to Argentina winning the 1986 World Cup

Argentina fans also displayed banners touting their country's claim to the Falkland Islands

Flares and fireworks were set off throughout the night, with barricades erected outside England’s team hotel to provide additional security.

Steve Borthwick’s side were due to return to the same hotel on Sunday, but Argentina’s progression to the final means the area is braced for more chaos.

The contest between the two sides comes just days after Argentina broke English hearts in the World Cup semi-finals on Wednesday.

Argentine fans attending the Nations Championship match were also seen displaying banners touting their country’s claim to the Falkland Islands.

FIFA is exploring disciplinary action against Argentina after several members of the team lifted a sign declaring 'Las Malvinas son Argentinas' - the country’s term for the South Atlantic islands.

The banner triggered a fierce backlash in the UK, with Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer saying he supports calls for FIFA to open an investigation made by Business Secretary Peter Kyle.

FIFA’s rules forbid the use of any political messaging at the World Cup but have previously turned a blind eye to continued references to the 1982 conflict in a song sung by the players – and posted on social media by the country’s association – in the dressing room throughout the tournament.

England were also mocked by Argentina star Enzo Fernandez, who shared a post on Instagram featuring a picture of him smiling alongside Lionel Messi and Leandro Paredes.

The post was accompanied by the Oasis hit Wonderwall, which had become the soundtrack to England's World Cup campaign in North America.

Sports.title: This dramatic victory keeps the knives at bay for Steve Borthwick but England have one glaring problem that they have to sort before they can challenge the world's best
Sports.content:
This dramatic victory keeps the knives at bay for Steve Borthwick but England have one glaring problem that they have to sort before they can challenge the world's best

Unlock more of the best of our [sport] coverage with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight and the writers you love every day

In the Plaza Libertad, hundreds of indigenous South Americans filed past England’s team hotel on Saturday morning for La Marcha de los Bombos. They blasted on ox horns and beat drums made from hollowed tree trunks in celebration of their ancestors.

Lose here and the jungle drums back at Twickenham would have been deafening for Steve Borthwick. They will continue to beat quietly into the autumn. This campaign has not been defiant enough to silence Borthwick’s many critics.

Jack van Poortvliet, Alex Coles, Henry Pollock, Emmanuel Iyogun were all sin-binned in the second half as England took their tally to 14 cards in 10 Tests. They have developed a reputation as one of the most ill-disciplined teams in Test rugby.

Two wins from three was the requirement for Borthwick to keep his job and his players desperately held on to keep the knives at bay. There was spirit in their final stand – down to 12-men at one point so they could form a scrum – and they celebrated with joyous relief by blasting out Sam Fender in the changing room.

If they are going to take on the world’s biggest hitters – of which Argentina are not one – then Borthwick must find a way to stop his team from buckling under pressure. They were saved by an agonisingly long frame-by-frame review in the final play, when Bautista Delguy’s try was overruled for being in touch. The hosts were furious, aghast that Noah Caluori was not penalised for a high tackle as England’s 13-men escaped.

On the sidelines, England’s players collapsed to the floor in relief at the final whistle. Their spirit has been battered in recent months. This tour has taken them to many corners of the world – three continents in three weekends. They have travelled 27,000 miles on 10 different flights and yet it feels like they have not moved too far forward.

England's Marcus Smith scores despite the efforts of Argentina's Santiago Carreras

Immanuel Feyi-Waboso was England’s game-breaker. Without their jet-heeled winger, England would probably have lost this match

It will be a tricky debrief for RFU CEO Bill Sweeney, who has been travelling through Argentina with the team. In many ways, his destiny feels intertwined with Borthwick’s. His tenure has already been smeared by three clubs going bust, failed governance reform, bonus scandals and terminating Eddie Jones’s contract. Replacing Borthwick would leave his own future in doubt.

Before kick-off, the stadium DJ blasted La Cuarta Estrella on the sound system. It is the song that the Argentinian football team have been playing all week. For Malvinas, for Diego, for Leo’s last. The Pumas even wore jerseys based upon the kit worn when Diego Maradona scored his Hand of God goal against England in 1986.

At one stage, this felt like this was going in a similar direction to Wednesday night’s World Cup semi-final. Borthwick’s side stormed to a 19-3 lead in the first-half but they ended with a fight to save their summer. They ended as a team who could not wait for the final whistle. They remain well behind South Africa and France.

Immanuel Feyi-Waboso was England’s game-breaker. Without their jet-heeled winger, England would probably have lost this match. He was the first player to demand the ball and made nine carries in the first half. England made the worst possible start against South Africa two weeks ago but here they hit the right notes in the first quarter.

A no-arms tackle by Marcos Kremer gifted England an early advantage and it took just four minutes to break the deadlock. Ollie Chessum conceded a penalty for antagonising Argentina during the celebrations but the English defence buckled up. Feyi-Waboso made a key tackle, Seb Atkinson forced a turnover and Marcus Smith dislodged the ball from the grasp of Mateo Carreras.

Feyi-Waboso’s England career has been riddled by injuries but here he reminded everyone of his world-class potential. His upper body strength got him out of tackles and his speed allowed him to burst clear, setting up Ben Earl to score the second try.

There was a purpose to England’s attack but, frustratingly, their search for a complete performance continues. They displayed a blueprint by offloading from the floor and keeping the ball alive in the first phase. Santi Carreras gave his team a foothold in the game with a penalty but England’s dominant scrum allowed Earl to score his second from a pushover try.

But in the second half, Argentina began to win the collisions. England slipped off tackles and their defence was stretched. When they came under pressure, England’s discipline collapsed.

In the second half, Argentina began to win the collisions and England’s discipline collapsed

England's wing Tommy Freeman scores after a lovely Fin Smith kick

Travel fatigue is a factor by this stage of the tour. The flight demands have been gruelling for England, who were thrown around by turbulence on their latest leg up from Buenos Aires. The logistics should be reviewed in future demands, although this was an opponent that England were expected to beat with ease.

Matteo Carreras scored from a pick and go early in the second half. Jack van Poortvliet slapped a pass down in desperation for the first yellow card, before Alex Coles swiped at an offload to concede a penalty try. Suddenly England had lost control.

Argentina suffered their own batch of yellow cards, reduced to 13-men when Santi Carreras tried to slap down the assisting pass for Marcus Smith’s try. Waboso’s score looked to have sealed the win but England folded once more.

Pollock and Iyogun were both sin-binned for running offside in the late defensive stand. Justo Picardo scored to set up a grandstand finale. Benhard Janse van Rensburg knocked himself out in the tackle, showing a defensive commitment that means the debate and uncertainty around England’s best midfield will rumble into the autumn.

Delguy thought he had scored a try to snatch a draw, but Henry Slade’s last-gasp tackle was judged to have brushed him into touch, potentially saving Borthwick’s job in the process.

Sports.title: Chelsea expected to complete stunning £117m Morgan Rogers deal as Blues swoop for Arsenal target
Sports.content:
Chelsea expected to complete stunning £117m Morgan Rogers deal as Blues swoop for Arsenal target

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Chelsea are expected to complete a £117million move for Morgan Rogers next week - a Premier League record for a British player.

Rogers has been one of Arsenal’s top targets throughout the summer but until now the Gunners have not met Villa’s valuation of their star attacker.

Arsenal had expected a clear run at Rogers, who has always been open to joining the Premier League champions. However, it was felt they moved too slowly after boss Mikel Arteta had met the player and Villa were unimpressed.

Daily Mail Sport understands Chelsea have entered the race and expect to complete a £117m move next week. He could have his medical as soon as Monday after returning from America with England, before signing a six-year contract.

Arsenal are huge admirers of Rogers, but they also have Bradley Barcola, the Paris Saint-Germain and France winger, high on their list.

Chelsea talent ID chief Joe Shields knows Rogers from his time at Manchester City, where the England attacker also played with current Blues players Cole Palmer and Tosin Adarabioyo.

Though Villa will play in the Champions League this season while Chelsea will not compete in Europe, it is thought this alone would not affect Rogers’ thinking.

Chelsea are expected to complete a £117million move for Morgan Rogers next week

Xabi Alonso's side have stolen a march on Arsenal, who had made Rogers a top target

Arsenal have also shown interest in Villa defender Ezri Konsa and an offer is on the cards - though there is some distance between the clubs’ valuations of the England centre-back.

If Rogers departs this summer, it would deprive Villa of a player who has produced double figures in goals and assists in the last two seasons.

With the club operating within strict margins after breaking UEFA spending rules, a record sale would boost the balance sheet and give boss Unai Emery the chance to make further signings.

Sports.title: Argentina fans spark wild World Cup scenes in New York as thousands take over Times Square - despite flash floods
Sports.content:
See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

New York's Times Square was transformed into a sea of blue and white on Saturday after Argentina fans took over the area ahead of this weekend's World Cup final.

As 'La Albiceleste' prepare to face off with Spain at New Jersey's MetLife Stadium in Sunday's showpiece event, thousands of fans swarmed upon the Big Apple.

In wild scenes captured by The Daily Mail, Argentina supporters were seen singing, dancing and waving flags as they partied in the rain at the New York landmark.

Despite New York battling through flash floods, that didn't appear to dampen the Argentina fans' spirits as they weathered the storm on Saturday afternoon.

The South American fans were clearly still reeling from their dramatic comeback against England in the tournament's semi-final on Wednesday evening.

Lionel Messi and Co. staged a late resurgence to book their place in Sunday's final, after scoring two goals in the dying moments to beat the Three Lions 2-1.

New York's Time Square was transformed into a sea of blue and white on Saturday after Argentina fans took over the area ahead of this weekend's World Cup final

Thousands of supporters swarmed to the iconic New York landmark one day before the final

Despite New York battling flash floods, that didn't dampen the mood for Argentina fans

England had taken the lead through winger Anthony Gordon in the 55th minute, before Enzo Fernandez and Lautaro Martinez struck for Argentina.

Meanwhile, Spain defeated France 2-0 in their respective semi-final - with Mikel Oyarzabal and Pedro Porro on the scoresheet for La Roja.

Sunday's final will see Barcelona legend Messi take on Spain's 19-year-old star Lamine Yamal - who once crossed paths in bizarre circumstances years ago.

Once their date with destiny was confirmed, a barely-believable photo of an astonishing encounter in 2007 resurfaced on social media this week.

The snap in question shows then-Barcelona star Messi, while carrying out a photoshoot for local newspaper Diario Sport and charity UNICEF, sitting on the floor to help to bathe the future Spain wonderkid in a blue plastic bathtub, before later cradling him while he's wrapped in a towel.

The pictures were posted on Instagram by Yamal's father, Mounir Nasraoui, in 2024 with the caption: 'The beginning of two legends.'

Two days before they meet in the World Cup final, Messi was asked about the extraordinary images of him with a young Yamal after appearing at Fanatics Fest in New York City.

'That picture, it was crazy. Him as a baby, and now we are facing each other... so once again what a crazy picture,' the soccer legend said when asked by NFL icon Tom Brady about the photos.

Thousands of fans were seen singing, dancing and chanting throughout the afternoon

Argentina fans made use of branded umbrellas as they battled the elements on Saturday

Lionel Messi admits the viral photo of him bathing a six-month-old Lamine Yamal is 'crazy'

Messi is set to collide with Yamal in the World Cup final, almost two decades after he helped bathe the future Spain wonderkid as a baby

'I just wish him the best of luck, and he's part of the Barcelona squad as well. We will try to give them [Spain] the best match possible, [but] Lamine is not the only great player that Spain has. So again we will give it our all.'

Before addressing the UNICEF photos, Messi described Yamal as 'one of the best players in the world right now.'

'He's only 19 years old and he has all of his future ahead. He has the opportunity to make history, but we are also going to give it our best,' he added.

Photographer Joan Monfort, who works as a freelance photojournalist for the AP, took the photos of Messi and Yamal in 2007 as part of a charity calendar produced by local newspaper Sport and UNICEF.

Sports.title: Argentina 24-31 England PLAYER RATINGS: Who came up with some massive hits for Steve Borthwick, who was 'devastating' star man and whose experience was key... but who only gets 4 out of 10?
Sports.content:
England won a thriller against Argentina, surviving a late comeback and seeing the hosts suffer a disallowed try at the death as Steve Borthwick's side ended their summer Nations Championship matches with a bang.

Borthwick's team looked to be in command going into the final stages after Ben Earl had scored twice and Immanuel Feyi-Waboso had lit up a match littered with yellow cards only for Argentina to score leaving them needing a converted try to draw. And they thought they had a try at the death only for the TMO to disallow it denying them a shot at levelling the Test.

Daily Mail Sport rugby writer Alex Bywater rates the players on a dramatic night in Argentina.

ENGLAND

15. Marcus Smith - 6.5

Spilled ball in wide channels. Forced into emergency scrum-half duty again as he was against Fiji but came up with crucial try.

Marcus Smith dives over the tryline to extend England's lead over Argentina in Santiago del Estero

14: Tommy Freeman - 7.5

Excellent finish from Fin Smith cross-kick. Must stay on the wing rather than be pushed back into the midfield.

13: Henry Slade - 8

Brilliant tackle on Delguy at the death won the game for England. Experience was key to helping navigate pressure.

12: Seb Atkinson - 6.5

Strong breakdown work and much more involved in attack than we’ve seen from him previously. Better intent to play to width.

11: Immanuel Feyi-Waboso - 8.5

Star man. Promising dash to start summed up very impressive outing. Fine try and showed how devastating a runner he can be.

England's Immanuel Feyi-Waboso makes yet another break against Argentina

10: Fin Smith - 7

Knock-on over the goal-line when try was there for the taking. Nice creativity and kicking otherwise. Temporarily forced off for head injury assessment.

9: Jack Van Poortvliet - 6.5

Forwards in front of him were on top. One sniping run. Yellow card for deliberate knock-on left England down to 14 again.

1: Ellis Genge - 7

Coughed up two scrum penalties but responded with a brutal carry in between. It was a surprise he was replaced so early by debutant Immanuel Iyogun who saw yellow.

2: Jamie George (capt) - 6.5

Targeted at the kick-off and penalised for obstruction but will be pleased with his team’s success in Argentina’s back yard.

ARGENTINA RATINGS

Sports.title: Oliver Glasner's to-do list: The gap in Nottingham Forest squad he's close to filling, keeping Evangelos Marinakis happy - and the line at his unveiling that set him apart from his predecessors
Sports.content:
Oliver Glasner's to-do list: The gap in Nottingham Forest squad he's close to filling, keeping Evangelos Marinakis happy - and the line at his unveiling that set him apart from his predecessors

Unlock more from Tom Collomosse inside the Forest camp with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight, analysis and more

Oliver Glasner has been at Nottingham Forest for only three days but already his in-tray is filling up.

The Austrian has five weeks to reconfigure his team’s tactics, establish who he can rely on and – crucially – identify his principal centre forward for the campaign ahead.

Glasner cut a relaxed figure when he was introduced to the media at the City Ground on Thursday, cracking jokes about his first date with his wife, but he knows the honeymoon period will be brief.

Daily Mail Sport looks at the main challenges facing Glasner as he tries to ensure his team hit the ground running when they face Leeds on August 22.

Oliver Glasner cut a relaxed figure at the City Ground on Thursday, cracking jokes about his first date with his wife, but he knows the honeymoon period will be brief

The Austrian has had huge success with a 3-4-2-1 system and it would be a surprise if he deviated from it significantly at Nottingham Forest

The missing pieces

At Crystal Palace, Glasner had huge success with a 3-4-2-1 system that proved hugely effective on the counter-attack – though breaking down defensive teams was often a problem.

He insists he has yet to decide between a back three and a back four and was at pains to say he does not want to create ‘Palace Two’ at Forest. Yet given the success he had in south London, it would be a surprise to see Forest line up radically differently.

Glasner intends to play with two No 10s behind a lone front man. Expect one of these to be Morgan Gibbs-White – assuming the Forest captain stays – with the other spot up for grabs. Forest are pursuing Tottenham midfielder Lucas Bergvall strongly.

Glasner namechecked Omari Hutchinson and James McAtee in his opening remarks, referencing Hutchinson’s ability to cut inside and shoot on his left foot. As long as Hutchinson has a decent pre-season, we can expect him to figure strongly in the early weeks of the new campaign.

Yet where Hutchinson improved as the season progressed, McAtee struggled throughout and made only 13 starts – two in the league. Just because McAtee is praised by the manager on July 16, that does not guarantee he will be at Forest when the summer window closes.

Perhaps, though, Glasner could be the coach to bring the best from McAtee, who is talented but suffers in the ultra-athletic modern game. If he has mentioned McAtee, it is because Glasner believes he can improve him.

Morgan Gibbs-White will almost certainly be one of Glasner's No10s behind the striker

Elliot Anderson was sold to Manchester City for £116million and Glasner accepts he cannot replace him with one player only. Xaver Schlager is set to join on a free transfer after leaving RB Leipzig and may line up alongside Ibrahim Sangare in the middle of the park, with the Ivory Coast star set to sign a new deal.

While there are plenty of defensive options, right back and No9 are key.

There is an acceptance at Forest that due to his injury record, Ola Aina needs a proven alternative, while Chris Wood turns 35 in December. Forest will be prepared to invest significantly in both areas, and Glasner sidestepped questions about whether he would target Palace players. Daniel Munoz and Jean-Philippe Mateta would certainly help this squad, though.

Glasner’s bold approach

Since Steve Cooper transformed Forest in 2021, leading them from the bottom of the Championship to promotion later that season, all managers have followed him in leaning heavily into Forest’s history.

The club won consecutive European Cups in 1979 and 1980 under Brian Clough, and memories of those days are on display across the City Ground. It would have been easy for Glasner to celebrate that as his predecessors did. He chose not to.

‘It’s a club with huge history but if we all lived as we did 46 years ago, we would fail,’ he said. ‘It’s good to have a great history but great history doesn’t tell anything about the future.

‘We want to make a step forward. Now is our fifth year in the Premier League and it doesn’t make sense talking about the European Cup trophies. Let’s get consistency into Forest in every way.’

It was a bold step and proves Glasner is not here to toe the line. Having won four major trophies (three with Palace and one with Frankfurt) Glasner has huge confidence in his own ability and is not afraid to show it.

Nor will he be afraid to put pressure on the ownership, or to make his feelings known if he is not given what he believes he needs. Indeed, there were plenty of clashes like these during his two-and-a-half years at Palace.

Unlike his predecessors, Glasner did not pay lip service to Forest's European Cup wins under Brian Clough

‘It’s important we stick to what we tell each other as it builds trust and we all want to feel that,’ said Glasner. ‘It’s like friendships or relationships. If someone tells you something and doesn't stick to their word, you don’t trust them anymore.’

Evangelos Marinakis does not mind the odd forthright back-and-forth with a manager and with Glasner, he will surely have his fair share.

Aiming high

Marinakis is the most ambitious owner in the Premier League, bar none. He believes Forest can break into the wealthy elite and become Champions League regulars. As Glasner acknowledged: ‘He is one of the few people I’ve met who are more ambitious than I am and that’s quite difficult. We will challenge each other with our ambition.’

It is very easy in July to talk about stability and consistency. It is a little more difficult if a club invests heavily and are 14th in the table at Christmas. Glasner pointed out that Forest’s league finishes had not always reflected their transfer spending and it is now for him to put that right.

In theory, Glasner’s brief will be to turn Forest into a club who compete regularly in the top half of the table and eventually push for Europe. In practice, he will be expected to hit the ground running.

Talented centre back Murillo will stay at the City Ground unless Forest receive an offer wildly above his market value

Unless they receive offers wildly above their market values, Forest have no plans to sell Gibbs-White, Neco Williams or Murillo. In return, Marinakis will expect no struggles in the bottom half of the table.

Glasner will not worry about these tasks. He has already chosen a difficult route by opting for Forest, who are disliked intensely by Palace these days after the Eagles were demoted to the Conference League a year ago due to UEFA rules, allowing Forest to step into the Europa League. He does not worry, he insists, about whether he’ll become Forest’s fifth managerial casualty in a relatively short time, after Nuno Espirito Santo, Ange Postecoglou, Sean Dyche and Vitor Pereira.

One word of advice, though, Oliver: get a couple of wins on the board early.

Sports.title: Team GB star Josh Kerr destroys remarkable 27-year-old world record
Sports.content:
Team GB star Josh Kerr destroys remarkable 27-year-old world record

Josh Kerr, who competes primarily in the 1,500 metres, had been targeting the record as part of what he called 'Project 222' - and today, his attempt in London was successful

View 4 Images Josh Kerr celebrates after breaking the world record for the mile (Image: Ali Habib/ZUMA Press Wire/Shutterstock)

Team GB star Josh Kerr has broken the 27-year-old world record for the mile at the London Diamond League.

‌



The 28-year-old middle-distance runner, who competes primarily in the 1,500 metres, clocked an astonishing three minutes and 42.66 seconds. Competing in front of a sold-out home crowd at the London Stadium at Queen Elizabeth Olympic Park, he took nearly half a second off Hicham El Guerrouj's legendary 27-year-old mark of 3:43.13.

‌



The retired Moroccan runner had set the record in 1999. With today's run, Kerr successfully fulfilled his highly publicised season-long campaign, "Project 222," named after the 222 seconds he targeted to run a 3:42 mile.

‌



Team GB star Charlotte Bankes represented another country at Winter Olympics before deserting them READ MORE :

World Cup winner calls on Donald Trump for help after visa rejected on eve of the final READ MORE :

View 4 Images He broke a world record in the Men's 1 Mile final at the London Stadium on July 18 (Image: Adam Davy/PA Wire)

Kerr finished more than three seconds ahead of US athlete Yared Nuguse, whose time was 3:45.69. "It was just incredible, that last lap," Kerr told the BBC.

"It was just me, my shoes and the track. I was absolutely deaf in the last 110 metres." He continued: "I didn't take my foot off the gas, but I started to glide and I was like 'oh wow this feels incredible.' It's incredible because I'm slowing down.

‌



"So, I was like 'I better get to the line'. So, crossing the finish line, seeing 42-something - anything - was my goal, so it was great." Despite breaking a world record, the runner said he hoped "it was going to be a little bit faster."

View 4 Images The runner had announced his record attempt in March (Image: Getty Images)

He added that the race was "very overwhelming" as "there was a lot of hype." He shared: "I am surrounded by amazing people and was just able to stay consistent, put the work in, and I knew I had 3:42 in me. I nearly lost it there at the end, but I got over the line."

‌



The runner continued: "If I'm to leave my mark on this sport as a British legend, with the legends behind me and following in their footsteps, I have to put in those performances."

Kerr's previous best before Saturday's run was 3:45.34. The athlete announced his world record attempt in March.

View 4 Images Thanks to Kerr, the mile record is back in British hands (Image: Action Plus/Shutterstock)

Article continues below

He said at the time: "For me, this wasn't an idea to hopefully save athletics but it is definitely a situation where 'why not?'. Why not go after something like this in front of as many people as possible?

"It's been a really fun journey and I like challenging myself. I like goals that are lofty and I think this sport needs moments, and I was willing to give it."

Saturday's win earned him a cheque for $50,000 (£37,000). Thanks to his win, the mile record is back in British hands after Roger Bannister became the first person to run under four minutes in 1954.

Sports.title: Thomas Tuchel called out for 'talking nonsense' before England vs France World Cup clash
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel called out for 'talking nonsense' before England vs France World Cup clash

Croatia great Davor Suker has criticised England manager Thomas Tuchel for his World Cup comments ahead of kick-off against France

View 2 Images Thomas Tuchel is underfire from Croatia great Davor Suker after his World Cup comments. (Image: Martin Rickett/PA Wire)

Croatia icon Davor Suker has taken aim at England manager Thomas Tuchel. The German head coach has received criticism following his comments ahead of the Three Lions' third-place play-off against France.

‌



England take on fellow beaten semi-finalists in Miami on Saturday (10pm kick-off) looking to bounce back from their devastating exit to Argentina. Tuchel came under fire for his tactics after his side squandered a one-goal lead against the reigning champions.

‌



Anthony Gordon had opened the scoring midway through the second-half before late goals from Enzo Fernandez and Lautaro Martinez turned the tie on its head. A demoralised England will have to lick their wounds against a France side who were brushed aside by Spain.

‌



However, Tuchel's comments about the battle for the wooden spoon haven't gone down well with Croatia as the 58-year-old took aim at the head coach.

Suker inspired the Vatreni to third-place in 1998, taking home the golden boot with six efforts.

Chelsea strike mega £117m Morgan Rogers transfer with Arsenal set to miss out on star READ MORE :

Arsenal transfer target told he wouldn’t get into Man Utd team in brutal verdict READ MORE :

He said: "I think the rich don't want to play when they lose. After 1998, when we played the Netherlands for third place, we fought for that bronze medal, and today I can still speak about it with pride.

‌



"Some people have won so many trophies and are so wealthy that this match means nothing to them.

"My message to them is: be quiet, respect all 211 participants, and understand that the world doesn't belong only to them. It belongs to the middle-sized nations, the smaller ones, and to everyone who loves football.

"Whoever wins third place tomorrow, I assure you that in 20 years, when they're older, they'll still remember that bronze medal. That's why, in this whole story, coach Tuchel doesn't matter. He's talking nonsense."

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

The former Chelsea and Bayern Munich head coach caused a stir during his pre-match duties with his comments surrounding the third-place playoff.

He said: "None of our players and none of the French players want to play this match. They want to play the final.

‌



"We gave everything to achieve that. Everyone plays to win the World Cup, but that’s how it is. We have one less day of recovery than France, but we will do it with professionalism."

View 2 Images Thomas Tuchel is underfire. (Image: FIFA via Getty Images)

Tuchel faces immense scrutiny over his future in the Three Lions hot-seat after coming in for severe criticism for their collapse against Argentina.

Article continues below

England were within 10 minutes of their second ever World Cup final but regressed and opted to move into a defensive shape that allowed the defending champions to capitalise and keep their hopes of retaining alive.

Sports.title: Jude Bellingham 'planning billionaire empire and knighthood' after 2026 FIFA World Cup
Sports.content:
Jude Bellingham 'planning billionaire empire and knighthood' after 2026 FIFA World Cup

Jude Bellingham and the England team may have lost out on 2026 World Cup glory - but the Real Madrid star stands to build far more lucrative prizes following his time on the pitch

View 4 Images Jude Bellingham has grand plans to build a billion pound brand (Image: (Photo by Dan Mullan/Getty Images))

Jude Bellingham plans to build up a billion-pound business empire - and even bag a knighthood - off the back of his World Cup success. Although the 23-year-old football star suffered the heartbreak of being kicked out of the 2026 Fifa contest when England lost against Argentina in the semi-finals, he has arguably become one of the big winners of the World Cup - snagging millions of new fans and becoming a bankable new star.

‌



Jude - who hails from Birmingham and currently plays for Real Madrid - left fans swooning as well as cheering as he scored an impressive six goals over the course of the tournament. The handsome star already landed lucrative endorsement deals with brands including Skims underwear and Lucozade long before the World Cup kicked off - and now stands to land even more deals thanks to his athletic antics on the pitch.

‌



With his profile skyrocketing, it is reported that Jude hopes to build a brand that could rival that of Sir David Beckham, who also saw his star power skyrocket while in his 20s, despite failing to win multiple World Cups. And it seems Becks has a career path that Jude hopes to emulate - knighthood and all.

‌



View 4 Images The Real Madrid player is said to be modelling his future success on that of David Beckham (Image: The FA via Getty Images)

A source told the Daily Mail: "It’s all been very hush-hush. But Jude knows his worth and what he can earn. The levels of hysteria over him can only be matched by David Beckham when he was in his early 20s."

The source continued: "Jude is very, very marketable and those around him know he can be a billionaire, and even a 'Sir', and that plan has just begun." The Daily Mail's report went on to suggest that Jude has boosted the team at Bello&Bello Ltd - the company that helps the England star monetise his image rights.

‌



Run by Jude, his mother Denise, father Mark and fellow footballer brother Jobe, Bello&Bello has reportedly expanded to include legal expert Oliver Hunt, a founding partner of Onside Law, financial advisor Simon Morris, and former Football Association players, led by Lewis Maddison, to help solidify the power of the limited company.

4 View 4 Images Jude has made millions thanks to endorsement deals with brands including Skims 4 View 4 Images Jude is dating American content creator Ashlyn Castro (Image: PA)

‌



The Daily Mail source claims: "Jude has a very carefully orchestrated plan in place. His parents have been so controlling of his career, but the decision was made that if he wants to grow bigger and become the next Beckham, he needs to put the infrastructure in place." The source goes on to state the team are working to build Jude's brand to become "Billionaire Bellingham". The Mirror has contacted Bello&Bello for comment.

Jude was a stand out player during the 2026 World Cup, scoring goals for his national team and winning fans for his sporting prowess and good looks in equal measure. Some fans may be disappointed to learn, however, that he is far from single.

The sportsman has been in a relationship with American influencer Ashlyn Castro, 28, since 2025 - with some reports suggesting they matched on elitist dating app Raya in 2024. Football fans have spotted Ashlyn watching Jude from the stands during the world cup - however the social media star has been targeted by cruel online trolls over her romance.

‌



Opening up about the impact online abuse has had on her, she told followers on TikTok: “I feel quite uneasy discussing my private life on camera. Please be patient with me as I’ve hardly done this before. I’ve encountered constant disrespect, abuse, and criticism from all sides. It’s been too much."

She continued: "Let's talk about this dating history. I've had three boyfriends over the last eight years. In 2017, I was in my very first relationship and he's a public figure, so because of that, I've dealt with people talking about me, making up things about me.

"There was nothing on the internet about me prior, so people kind of just made up a bunch of things to justify hating me because of who I was dating at the time. And then over the last six years after that, I've dated two people. So three relationships in total."

Article continues below

And she added: "I'm like shaking because I'm not ready to talk about this on the internet. This is extremely personal. This is my real life. I shouldn't have to talk about this. But moving forward I will talk about things that are important such as mental health. This is something that I wanted to use my platform for but I just wasn't ready."

Sports.title: Drake leaves fans thinking Spain will win FIFA World Cup 2026 after 'curse'
Sports.content:
Drake leaves fans thinking Spain will win FIFA World Cup 2026 after 'curse'

Argentina will face Spain in the 2026 Fifa World Cup final on Sunday - but betting fans are now convinced the European nation will win thanks to a bet placed by Canadian rap star Drake

View 5 Images Drake is said to be cursed when it comes to placing bets on sporting events (Image: Getty Images)

Football fans have become convinced Argentina will lose the 2026 FIFA World Cup - after rap star Drake placed a bet they will win. On Sunday night, the South American nation will face off against Spain for a chance to win the golden trophy.

‌



But superstitious sport fans think Argentina has been given the kiss of death after being backed by Canadian music sensation Drake. The 39-year-old chart-topping star has a track record for backing the wrong side and placing bets on teams or sporting personalities that then go on to lose.

‌



Football fans are now sure that Spain will scoop the Fifa trophy after the Hotline Bling singer placed a $1.5 million (£1.12 million) bet that Lionel Messi's team would win the cup. If Drake is correct, he stands to win a huge $5.1 million prize (£3.8 million).

‌



View 5 Images The Canadian musician boasted about placing a huge bet on Argentina winning (Image: Instagram/ @champagnepapi)

Taking to social media ahead of the hotly anticipated World Cup final, Drake shared a screenshot showing he had placed a big-money bet on Argentina to win. The bet is proof enough for many that the Spanish team - captained by Rodrigo Hernández Cascante, known as Rodri or Rodrigo - will win instead.

Taking to social media, many sports fans have turned to mocking Drake over his betting choice - and highlighted the bad string of bets he has recently placed. One fan on X, formerly known as Twitter, typed: "Argentina's toughest opponent isn't Spain, it's Drake's $1.5M Stake bet."

‌



And another sports fan joked on X: "Damnit. Just when I went big on [Argentina]. Might have to cash out." Earlier this month, Drake appeared to prove himself a bad source of betting advice.

View 5 Images Football fans are now convinced Lionel Messi and his team will now lose the tournament

He revealed on social media that he placed a $1 million (£740,000) bet on Conor McGregor winning his UFC comeback fight. However, the Irish fighter injured himself in the first round and then suffered a TKO loss.

‌



Drake's string of betting bad luck has even led to the creation of a website called TheDrakeCurse.com, which has been keeping track of his terrible betting choices. The website claims that the music star - who has also produced hit TV shows including Top Boy for Netflix and Euphoria for HBO - has lost $1.56 million (£1.16 million) thanks to 87 bad bets.

Drake is far from the only person to have a flutter on the 2026 World Cup - with financial services firm Macquarie claiming the sporting contest is on track to become the biggest gambling event of all time. They estimate that approximately $50 billion (£37.1 billion) has been placed on bets for the football event.

5 View 5 Images Robbie Williams will perform at the 2026 Fifa World Cup final (Image: Getty Images) 5 View 5 Images Madonna is also due to perform at the 2026 Fifa World Cup final (Image: madonna/Instagram)

‌



This averages to $500 million (£371 million) being bet on each match, with the contest set to conclude on Sunday night with the Argentina v Spain final.

Chad Beynon, an analyst at Macquarie, explained to the BBC that in-play betting had dramatically changed the way gambling fans were placing bets, which traditionally involved putting your money down ahead of a match. He told the outlet: "Now it's all about reacting to what you're seeing on the field, adjusting your views. Whereas before it was kind of sit, watch, wait - you had to place your bet before the match."

The 2026 World Cup final is set to take place at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey, near New York City in the United States, on Sunday night, with kick-off expected at 8pm UK time. The finale is expected to be packed full of entertainment beyond the sport taking place on the pitch.

Article continues below

A closing ceremony will take place ahead of the first whistle, with performances by Laura Pausini, Nicole Scherzinger, Robbie Williams, IShowSpeed, and Jennifer Hudson. And for the first time, there will be a half-time show spectacle, which is tipped to run for 18 minutes.

Music legend Madonna will take to the ceremony to belt out songs - with Shakira, BTS and Justin Bieber also expected to perform. The glitzy final is expected to raise $100 million (£740,000) for the FIFA Global Citizen Education Fund.

Sports.title: Chelsea strike mega £117m Morgan Rogers transfer with Arsenal set to miss out on star
Sports.content:
Chelsea strike mega £117m Morgan Rogers transfer with Arsenal set to miss out on star

Arsenal had long been considered favourites in the race to sign Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa but the England star could now join their London rivals, Chelsea

View 2 Images Morgan Rogers looks to be Chelsea-bound (Image: Getty)

Chelsea are on the cusp of sealing a blockbuster £117million deal for Morgan Rogers in what would be one of the summer's biggest transfers.

‌



Rogers, 23, has emerged as one of the most sought-after attackers in Europe after another dazzling season with Aston Villa and was always expected to move for a significant transfer fee after the World Cup.

‌



Arsenal had seemed to be the most likely destination for the former Middlesbrough star and are known to be huge admirers of Rogers.

‌



But it is Chelsea who have now struck a verbal agreement to sign Rogers for a fee of £117m, with the player relishing the prospect of linking up with Chelsea's new manager, Xabi Alonso.

Arsenal transfer target told he wouldn’t get into Man Utd team in brutal verdict READ MORE :

With Stamford Bridge emerging as Rogers' preferred destination after talks with Alonso, the player has already agreed terms on a six-year contract and a medical is pencilled in for Monday.

Rogers started and notched an assist in England's heartbreaking World Cup semi-final defeat to Argentina and could be in action again tonight in the third-place play-off with France.

‌



The transfer will trigger a huge windfall for Rogers former club, Middlesbrough, who included a 20 per cent sell-on clause into the deal which took the attacking midfielder to Villa Park for an initial £7m with a further £8m in add-ons back in the 2024 winter window.

View 2 Images Rogers was in sensational form for Aston Villa last season (Image: Getty)

Landing Rogers is the first major win for Alonso, who agreed to become Chelsea's new manager earlier this year.

‌



The Spaniard will attempt to restore Chelsea's position in the upper echelons of the Premier League and get them challenging for major honours again following a challenging 2025-26 campaign which saw them finish 10th.

Rogers should further enhance Chelsea's attacking output after accumulating 14 goals and 12 assists across 55 games for Aston Villa last season in all competitions, helping them win the Europa League.

Not only will Rogers become Chelsea's club-record signing, with the deal surpassing the £107m agreement that brought Enzo Fernandez to Stamford Bridge, but he will also become the most expensive British footballer of all time ahead of his England colleague, Elliot Anderson.

Sports.title: Rory McIlroy rips into Bryson DeChambeau and accuses him of 'holding The Open hostage'
Sports.content:
Rory McIlroy rips into Bryson DeChambeau and accuses him of 'holding The Open hostage'

Rory McIlroy has hit out at Bryson DeChambeau's reaction to his two-shot penalty at The Open Championship, slamming the American in a sensational outburst

View 2 Images Rory McIlroy didn't hold back on Bryson DeChambeau after the American stole the headlines on Friday. (Image: Cameron Jourdan/X)

Rory McIlroy has slammed Bryson DeChambeau following his Open Championship antics. The world number two issued a damning assessment on the LIV Golf star, accusing his rival of taking the tournament 'hostage' during Friday's two-shot penalty controversy.

‌



The two-time Masters champion didn't hold back as he weighed in on the controversy surrounding the American. DeChambeau was found to have "inadvertently improved his swing" as he tackled the overgrown grass on the fringe of the fifth hole.

‌



He had carded seven under following Friday's second round, leaving trailing overnight leader Lucas Herbert by a single stroke, until the R&A intervened and determined that he had improved his lie on the fifth hole, which resulted in a two-shot penalty.

‌



Bryson DeChambeau breaks silence after The Open two-shot penalty amid quit fears READ MORE :

McIlroy disclosed that he witnessed the incident play out from the players' lounge and that the initial action aroused suspicions among the Northern Irishman and his fellow competitors. He said: "I was watching it live, I was up in the players' lounge with a few of the other players.

"As soon as he made the step into the ball, we all sort of looked at each other and were like, 'That didn't seem right'. When I heard that he'd been pulled in by the rules officials, I think it was obvious for why.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



"I think there's no doubt he improved the line of his backswing, whether it was careless or if it was intentional, it doesn't matter, hopefully was careless. I think the two-shot penalty was justified."

Players who made the cut and were scheduled to compete in Saturday's third round found themselves waiting around for their tee times.

The saga dragged on with all attention fixed on the officials' hut, where deliberations were underway before DeChambeau emerged onto the driving range shortly afterwards once the penalty had been confirmed.

‌



View 2 Images Bryson DeChambeau appeared to be suffering from a hangover following his Open Championship, controversy during his third round. (Image: Getty Images)

McIlroy added: "It was a late night for everyone. I won't pretend to up here and defend Bryson, I'm not particularly fond of him, a lot of it is performative, attention.

"To hold the tournament hostage like that, have players, volunteers and everyone within to the part, it wasn't a great look. I'm not in his mind but it didn't look good."

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"
